title: CTrees global aboveground biomass, 100 m annual (Icechunk)
description:
ctrees.org global annual aboveground biomass (AGB) at 100 m, 2000-2025, published as a bare Icechunk 2.x repository (a `repo` config object plus `chunks/`, `manifests/`, `snapshots/` prefixes -- confirmed by a 200 on the `repo` object; there is no `zarr.json`/`.zattrs` at this path because Icechunk stores its own metadata inside the repo, not as plain Zarr files). CORS confirmed (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on the S3 bucket). bbox is estimated (global biomass coverage, excluding high latitudes where AGB is not mapped); the grid itself is a full [-180, -90, 180, 90].

CORRECTION (browser run, 2026-11): the arrays WERE inspected, by opening the repository with `icechunk-js` 0.6.1 in node -- which reads this 2.x layout without trouble, and reports spec version 2. The store nests its data one group down, under `aboveground_biomass`, so the variables below name their full paths; with no `cube:variables` at all the browser found no array to render and reported the store as having no spatial reference. Values are raw int16 with `agb_scale_factor` 10 and `_FillValue` -9999, so the render rescales raw DN.

License unknown; declared "proprietary" with a via link.

Expected browser outcome: draws (viridis ramp on AGB) from zoom level 8. One level, no overviews: 405,000 cells across in 2,000-cell chunks is 203 chunks across the world, so the browser holds it back with the no-overviews zoom notice until then.

time.description: Annual, 2000-2025 (26 steps), confirmed from the array shape.

aboveground_biomass/agb.description: Shape [26, 202500, 405000]. Raw int16; `agb_scale_factor` 10, so a raw 3000 is 300 Mg/ha. CRS from the `aboveground_biomass/spatial_ref` array (`crs_wkt`, EPSG:4326).

data.title: CTrees AGB 100m global (Icechunk 2.x repository)
data.description: Icechunk spec version 2, opened with icechunk-js 0.6.1. Arrays under the `aboveground_biomass` group, with 1-D `x`/`y` float64 coordinates and a `spatial_ref` grid-mapping array.
